## Def1 - Installing Node Packages

### Def
The most common usage of `npm install` is to install packages listed in the `package.json` file of a Node.js project.

### CTP
When executed in a directory containing a `package.json` file, `npm install` reads the file and installs all the dependencies listed under `dependencies` and `devDependencies`.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install
```

::: {.callout-note}
If `package-lock.json` exists, `npm install` will install the exact versions specified in that file to ensure consistency across environments.
:::

## Installing a Specific Package

### Def
Used to install a specific package that is not already listed in `package.json`.

### CTP
This command adds the package to `node_modules` and updates the `package.json` and `package-lock.json` files with the new dependency.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install lodash
```

## Installing a Package Globally

### Def
Installs a package globally, making it available across all Node.js projects.

### CTP
Global installations do not modify the `package.json` or `package-lock.json` of the current project. Instead, the package is installed in a global directory.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install -g eslint
```

## Installing a Specific Version of a Package

### Def
Allows installation of a specific version of a package.

### CTP
This is useful when a specific version of a package is required for compatibility reasons.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install lodash@4.17.21
```

## Installing Packages from a URL

### Def
Installs a package directly from a URL, such as a GitHub repository.

### CTP
This can be useful for installing packages that are not available on the npm registry.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install https://github.com/user/package.git
```

## Installing Packages from a Local Directory

### Def
Installs a package from a local directory on the filesystem.

### CTP
This is useful for testing or using packages that are not yet published to the npm registry.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install ./path/to/package
```

## Installing Packages with a Prefix

### Def
Installs packages with a custom prefix, which can be useful for managing multiple versions of Node.js or npm.

### CTP
This changes the default directory where npm installs global packages.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install -g --prefix=/custom/path lodash
```

## Installing Peer Dependencies

### Def
Installs peer dependencies required by a package.

### CTP
Some packages rely on peer dependencies, which need to be installed manually or can be installed automatically with the `--include=peer` flag.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install --include=peer some-package
```

## Installing Packages with a Specific Version Range

### Def
Installs a package within a specified version range.

### CTP
This allows flexibility in specifying the version of a package that can be installed.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install lodash@">=4.0.0 <5.0.0"
```

## Installing Packages with a Dry Run

### Def
Simulates an installation without actually installing the packages.

### CTP
Useful for testing and verifying what packages and versions will be installed.

### Ex 
```{bash}
npm install --dry-run
```
